title: Liczby porządkowe · godziny
note: Two halves, deliberately kept apart. (1) Ordinals 1st-12th. a1_numbers already owns pierwszy, drugi, trzeci, czwarty, piaty (its time_numbers_tens block), so ONLY szosty, siodmy, osmy, dziewiaty, dziesiaty, jedenasty, dwunasty are taught here; the first five are recycled and listed in uses_lemmas. (2) Whole-hour clock time as FROZEN CHUNKS. LOCATIVE QUARANTINE: 'o trzeciej' is a feminine locative agreeing with an unspoken godzinie. That machinery is NOT taught here and must not be. Exactly the a2_shopping_func 'Place karta' treatment is applied: the case is never named, never explained, and no locative structure id is tagged on any o-time item. The ONLY statement made about the shape is the permitted one - the clock words all end in -ej and are learned whole. Critically, the pack NEVER contrasts an o-form with its plain ordinal: no item, explain, table row or quiz choice ever puts szosty next to o szostej, and every quiz choice touching an o-form is a WHOLE PHRASE set against other whole phrases (o siodmej / o szostej / o osmej), never a four-way ending drill, which would open the case by the back door. In type_items the ordinals are grouped first and the o-forms second so the two sets are never juxtaposed number-for-number. FENCED, must not appear anywhere: wpol do, za pietnascie, kwadrans po, any minutes-past-the-hour, any half-past or quarter form. All of those need genitive machinery plus a different clock logic (Polish counts toward the next hour) and are a separate unit. Whole hours only. ALSO FENCED: the feminine nominative answer set (Jest trzecia / Jest godzina trzecia). That is a THIRD inflected set on top of the ordinals and the -ej chunks, and the load-splitting rule forbids it here - so the unit teaches the learner to ASK the time and to SAY when things happen, and defers saying the hour back. FORKS, all reported: (a) 'O ktorej?' was added beyond the brief's list - it is in this node's own tree note, and without it the twelve -ej chunks have no natural prompt; it is taught whole exactly like 'Ktora godzina?', and 'ktorej' is tagged so the auditor sees it. (b) Both the bare -ej token (siodmej) and the full chunk (o siodmej) are tagged in teaches_lemmas, following the a2_shopping_func precedent of tagging both 'karta' and 'place karta'. (c) 'po poludniu' is NOT used anywhere: a1_time_cal taught only the noun popoludnie and 'po poludniu' is not in POOL. Verified and available for anchoring instead: rano, wieczorem, dzisiaj, jutro, wczoraj, codziennie. (d) a1_trunk_there_time (path 41, live) contains 'Ktora jest godzina?', 'Jest trzecia', 'Wstaje o siodmej' and 'od dziewiatej do piatej' as frames, but that pack carries NO teaches_lemmas, so none of those forms are in POOL - they are treated as untaught here and 'Ktora godzina?' is taught properly. 'od ... do ...' is not touched: od is untaught. All verbs imperfective. Every 3sg used (jest, ma, pije, kupuje, idzie, jedzie) is in POOL; wraca and wstaje are NOT in POOL and are deliberately absent.

intro.title: Ordinals: first, second, third…
intro.body:
Cardinals count how many — jeden, dwa, trzy. Ordinals name the position — first, second, third. Polish has a separate word for each, and it behaves like an adjective.

The first five are already yours from your numbers work. Seven are new, and only those seven are drilled in this unit.

Two to watch. Ósmy and siódmy both carry ó, which is simply the u sound — say oosmy and syoodmy. And the ordinal of twelve is dwunasty, not dwanasty: the cardinal dwanaście changes its middle when it becomes an ordinal. Jedenaście does not, so jedenasty is straightforward.
intro.body_pl: Liczby porządkowe: pierwszy, drugi, trzeci, czwarty, piąty, szósty, siódmy, ósmy, dziewiąty, dziesiąty, jedenasty, dwunasty.

intro.title: The clock: twelve phrases, learned whole
intro.body:
To say when something happens, Polish puts o in front of a clock word. You already know o from o domu, o pracy — here it is doing a different job, and the word after it is a fixed phrase.

Every clock word ends in -ej. That is the whole of what you need to notice about their shape. Do not try to build them out of anything, and do not change them. Learn each phrase whole, exactly as it stands — the same way you learned Płacę kartą.

Twelve phrases, one for each hour. Polish uses the same twelve for morning and evening in ordinary speech, so o ósmej covers eight in the morning and eight at night; rano and wieczorem sort it out when it matters.
intro.body_pl: Godziny w całości: o pierwszej, o drugiej, o trzeciej, o czwartej, o piątej, o szóstej, o siódmej, o ósmej, o dziewiątej, o dziesiątej, o jedenastej, o dwunastej.

intro.title: Asking the time, and asking when
intro.body:
Two questions, both fixed phrases.

Która godzina? = "What time is it?" Godzina is the hour, a word you have had since your calendar lessons. Put przepraszam in front of it and you can stop a stranger in the street.

O której? = "At what time?" This is the one that pairs with everything on the last slide: ask O której?, and the answer comes back as one of your twelve phrases.

— O której? — O trzeciej.

This unit stops at whole hours. Half past and quarter past work differently in Polish and they wait for their own unit.
intro.body_pl: Która godzina? O której? — O trzeciej.

rows: Excuse me, what time is it?

examples.en: Excuse me, what time is it?

intro.title: Putting the hour into a sentence
intro.body:
The clock phrase goes at the end of the sentence and nothing else has to move. Every one of these sentences is built from words you already produce — only the hour is new.

Add rano or wieczorem after it when the half of the day matters, and codziennie in front when it happens every day.
intro.body_pl: Pociąg jest o siódmej. Tata ma spotkanie o dziesiątej. Codziennie jem obiad o pierwszej.

examples.en: The film is at eight in the evening.
Dad has a meeting at ten.
Mum drinks coffee at nine in the morning.
examples.pl: Mama pije kawę o dziewiątej rano.

examples.en: Every day I eat lunch at one.

quiz.explain: Szósty carries ó, which is just the u sound: shoosty. Piąty is fifth and it is already yours, so it is the one you can rule out first.
Siedem is the cardinal — it counts how many. Siódmy names the position.
The word opens on ó, so it starts with the u sound: oosmy. Nothing else about it is unusual.
Ninth and tenth sound alike and sit next to each other. Nine has the nasal ą in the middle: dziewiąty. Ten does not.
Dziesięć is the cardinal you already have. The ordinal keeps the s of dziesięć — dziewiąty, ninth, has a w there instead.
Jedenaście is the cardinal. The ordinal swaps its tail for -asty and changes nothing else.
Watch the middle. The cardinal is dwanaście but the ordinal is dwunasty — dwu-, not dwa-. It is the only ordinal in this set that changes shape like that.
All four are real clock phrases and all four end in -ej. That ending tells you nothing about which hour it is — the middle of the word does.
O drugiej is at two. Dwunastej is the twelve one — take the phrase whole and there is nothing to work out.
The sentence never changes — only the fixed clock phrase at the end of it does.
Która godzina? asks what the time is now. O której? asks when something happens — a different question with a different answer.
This is the question your twelve clock phrases answer: — O której? — O trzeciej.

type_items.explain: The ó is the u sound, so this comes out as syoodmy. It is written ó and never u.
The word begins on ó — the u sound. Oosmy.
Ninth and tenth differ by one letter in the middle: dziewiąty has w, dziesiąty has s — the same s as in dziesięć.
Not dwanasty. The cardinal dwanaście changes its middle to dwu- when it becomes an ordinal, and this is the only word in the set that does it.
A fixed phrase, taken whole. Every clock word ends in -ej and there is nothing in it for you to build.
Written with ó, said with the u sound: o syoodmey.
Two o sounds run together here — o oosmey. Polish is happy with that and does not join them up.
Midday or midnight — the phrase is the same either way, and rano or wieczorem sorts it out if it matters.

use_items.explain: This is the pair the whole unit is built on: ask O której?, answer with one fixed clock phrase and nothing else.

use_items.explain: Polish uses the same twelve clock phrases day and night, so wieczorem is what tells you this is not eight in the morning.

use_items.explain: Spotkanie is neuter, so it looks the same after ma as it does on its own. The clock phrase simply sits at the end.
